name: reference_profile
hypothesis: Deriving a training-only reference profile (verbatim label vocabulary, answer shape and separators, question families with their recurring answer parts), ranking references by similarity with the question's family first, and forcing a check_answer pass on the draft before submitting raises the mean validation score above the 0.428 baseline, mainly by removing surface-form label mismatches on label-like tasks and multi-part under-prediction, without regressing tasks that have no label vocabulary.

name: atomic_reference_units
hypothesis: Validating each candidate separator by whether the pieces it produces are attested as complete reference answers (instead of by raw frequency), and cutting the label inventory only at validated separators, stops the profile from presenting fragments of a single reference answer as authoritative labels; the solver then answers with whole reference units, which raises mean validation accuracy above the 0.550 of iteration 1, mainly by converting label truncations into exact matches, without regressing tasks that have no label vocabulary.

name: considered_unit_audit
hypothesis: Presenting the reference units as evidence rather than a closed vocabulary, and re-opening in check_answer every candidate unit the solver named but did not submit (with the reference cases that answer each of them, ranked so units related to the draft come first), makes the solver keep the units it already found: the mean validation score rises above the 0.558 of iteration 2, mainly by converting dropped-but-correct units and near-miss substitutions (a broader listed unit put in place of the correct more specific one, or the reverse) into submitted ones, without regressing the tasks that have no unit vocabulary.

name: precedent_audit
hypothesis: Selecting the units the pre-submit check re-opens by how well this question matches the reference cases that answer them (instead of by corpus frequency), naming the element that separates a draft unit from its attested relative so the facts rather than the commoner label decide, flagging draft units that are only one element of a reference unit, and matching the question's own recurring type wherever its header appears in the input, lifts the mean validation score above the 0.584 of iteration 3 by raising the weak side of the multi-unit task (recall 0.680 against precision 0.760, no sample over-predicting), without regressing the single-unit and free-form tasks.

name: act_ledger_audit
hypothesis: Generating the candidate set from the question's own acts (a ledger of one entry per separate act or component the facts establish, each carrying the unit it calls for) instead of choosing among the reference units, and auditing the draft against that ledger rather than against the reference vocabulary - reporting every entry with no unit in the draft, quoting the closest reference case that answers with more parts when an entry is open, refusing to report the same unit relation twice so the check cannot oscillate between two related units, and inverting the rule to 'alternatives for one slot' when every reference answer is a single part - raises the mean validation score above the 0.584 of iteration 3, mainly by converting strict-subset answers on the multi-unit task into complete ones, without regressing the single-part and free-form tasks.

name: settled_draft_audit
hypothesis: Auditing only mechanical defects (markup, structure, fragments of attested units, near-miss spellings) and having the pre-submit check affirm a draft it finds nothing wrong with raises the mean validation score above the 0.584 of iteration 3, mainly by recovering the single-answer samples lost to the candidate-enumeration wording (0.89 back to 0.92) and the generation samples lost to it4/it5 relation steering and over-decomposition (USPTO 0.217 back to 0.283), without losing the multi-unit gain (LawBench at or above 0.58), because no iteration measured the re-open channel repairing a sample.

name: attested_rendering_audit
hypothesis: Reporting only attested renderings in the pre-submit check (a draft unit that is a piece of a reference unit, or an extension of one of its pieces, is answered with the whole unit the references render; markup is required only when the question states it; the re-open channel is deleted) while keeping the fact-based candidate wording raises the mean validation score above the 0.584 of iteration 3 - mainly by turning piece-of-a-unit drafts into whole attested units on the label task (7 of 100 samples, 0 of 160 on the other two tasks) and by removing the check's own noise (bracketed atoms demanded as markup, oscillating relation notes) - without regressing the single-label and free-form tasks.

name: family_shape_audit
hypothesis: Deriving a question type as the complete opening sentence several references share - and looking it up anywhere in the text the memory receives, since at solve time that text is the whole task prompt - so that the pre-submit check reports the answer count of the question's own type and treats a count that type never uses as a defect, with the verdict affirming a draft only when the report has nothing to say about it, raises the mean validation score above the 0.573 of iteration 7 and the 0.584 of iteration 3, mainly by turning drafts whose count their own type never uses into drafts with that type's count (2 replayed free-form drafts, both wrong, in a type that answers with 2 parts in 100% while the draft had 3) and by no longer talking a correct draft out of a unit it had already added (1 replayed label draft whose gold answer was exactly the draft the old relation note rejected), without regressing the tasks that have no question type, where the profile, the references and the check report are unchanged.

name: attested_retrieval_scale

name: cardinality_branch
hypothesis: Deriving from the training references whether the task answers with a single unit or with several (the share of reference answers that are one unit, closed at 0.98, measured as 1.00/0.685/0.36 on the three corpora) and making the system prompt, the skill's decision step and the check follow that derivation - on a one-unit corpus the solver chooses between the candidates it named instead of accumulating them, a re-opened candidate can only replace the draft's unit, and a two-unit draft is reported as a defect rather than a more complete answer - raises the mean validation score above iteration 3's 0.584 and iteration 10's 0.573, mainly by returning the single-unit task from 0.89 to its iteration-1/2 level of 0.91-0.92, whose wrong samples are substitutions between listed units rather than coverage gaps, without moving the multi-unit and free-form tasks, whose system prompt, rendered skill, guide and check output are byte-identical to iteration 3's (verified by re-rendering both and by replaying 169 recorded check_answer calls, 0 of which differ).

name: carry_offer
hypothesis: Reporting every candidate the draft does not carry as a defect of the draft, together with the answer written out as it would read if it carried it (the question's markup, the corpus's join separator, a replacement when the candidate contains the draft's units), and naming the reasons that do not rule a candidate out (the vocabulary not listing it, the references usually answering with one unit, another unit covering the same acts), converts more of the named-and-dropped candidates than the question form did - 7 of the 23 wrong questions on the corpus that answers with several units are of that kind and about one converted - while removing the corpus's modal answer-width percentage and its more/fewer-parts clauses stops the frequent count from being used as a reason to drop a unit; the multi-unit task rises above its 0.56-0.59 band, the free-form task stays inside 0.20-0.28, and the single-unit task does not move (its channel keeps the remark framing, because there a candidate competes with the answer rather than being missing from it).

name: fact_ruled_set
hypothesis: On a corpus whose reference answers are sets of vocabulary units (label-like and not single-unit; the third branch the profile's two measures separate), making the decision step set a unit aside only for a fact of the question, quoted from it, and naming the reasons that do not rule one out (another unit covering the same conduct, that unit being the more specific one, the conduct being fully evaluated by the draft's unit) - together with rendering a candidate that a draft unit is a variant of as a replacement rather than a join, and repairing a submission whose final_answer cannot be read - converts more of the 15 samples that a missing unit alone makes wrong than the 2 the candidate channel can reach, so that corpus rises above its 0.54-0.59 band while the one-unit corpus stays in 0.85-0.92 and the free-form corpus in 0.20-0.30, whose prompt and check output are byte-identical to iteration 12's.

name: attested_delimiters
hypothesis: The check reads every bracketed token in the question as markup the answer must carry, so 9 of 30 free-form questions (bracket atoms in the input SMILES) and 2 of 200 set-answering ones (a year in brackets) are told to fix a defect the question never asked for; 12 of 60 recorded free-form samples carry that false defect, 7 of them correct answers.
